title: Timed-out child with stderr-only output loses diagnostics

answer.patch:
--- a/util/subprocess_timeout.py
+++ b/util/subprocess_timeout.py
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@ def subprocess_with_hard_timeout(
         proc.wait(timeout=10)
         stdout = e.stdout if e.stdout else ""
         stderr = e.stderr if e.stderr else ""
-        if str(stdout).strip():
+        if stdout or stderr:
             return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                 args=cmd,
                 returncode=-9,
answer.reason: The original code only returned a CompletedProcess on timeout if stdout was non-empty. If the subprocess only wrote to stderr before timing out, it raised a bare ProcTimeout exception, losing the stderr diagnostics. Changing the condition to check for either stdout or stderr ensures the CompletedProcess is returned with the captured stderr whenever any output exists.
